critical_dependencies.dependency: SQLAlchemy ORM and session management for all persistent state.
stellium 0.13.0 plus local stellium_engine.py for chart and aspect calculations.
structlog for trace-friendly logs with block_id, report_id, client_id, and user identifiers.
Pydantic models for API/request validation and section schemas.
YooKassa SDK for subscription and credit payments.
OpenRouter HTTP access or locally authenticated Gemini/Codex CLIs for report/feed LLM generation.
WeasyPrint and markdown helpers for report rendering assets and print-ready output paths.

operational_constraints.constraint: Auth is header-based via X-Telegram-Auth and reused for admin gating; no cookie session contract is present.
docker-compose.yml sets DEFAULT_LLM_MODE=stub for backend by default; real LLM operation requires explicit provider credentials or mounted CLI homes.
Backend startup performs additive runtime migrations and starts the in-process scheduler; schema drift must be treated cautiously.
Frontend proxy routes depend on INTERNAL_API_URL or NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL resolving to backend.
Playwright browsers are not installed in the normal frontend dev container; canonical E2E runs only through the Playwright container wrapper.
Notification delivery is best-effort over the bot internal HTTP service and must not be a hard dependency for transaction completion.
Weekly horary quota depends on user-local timezone calculation, falling back to UTC when timezone is absent or invalid.
Admin server actions currently have auth gaps in the snapshot; treat admin UI changes as high-risk until DEFECT-ADMIN-SERVER-AUTH is resolved.

environment_assumptions.assumption: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is available for both bot runtime and Telegram auth verification.
DATABASE_URL points to PostgreSQL and matches sync usage in backend and async usage in bot.
BOT_ADMIN_IDS defines the admin allowlist for backend admin endpoints and bot notifications.
YOOKASSA_SHOP_ID and YOOKASSA_SECRET_KEY are optional in local/mock mode but required for real billing.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY or CLI credentials are present when DEFAULT_LLM_MODE or FEED_LLM_MODE is not stub/mock/fallback.
Runtime migrations in backend/app/db.py are the current schema mechanism; there is no separate canonical Alembic flow in the reviewed slice.

business_verification_mechanism.mechanism: Use deterministic response shapes plus trace evidence from structlog events such as report.async.start, report.gen.start, report.section.done, billing.success, referral.partner_reward, feed.generated, and scheduler.*.
Correlate evidence by report_id, client_id, section_id, telegram_id, and block_id where present.
For UI flows, use Playwright container runs against the webapp while preserving Telegram auth/header assumptions.
